facts.t: The Supreme Court banned a school textbook it appeared in
facts.d: In Re: NCERT Class 8 Textbook was taken up suo motu with no petitioner, over a chapter referencing judicial corruption and backlog. The Court ordered seizure and digital takedown — and was criticised for acting as both protector and prosecutor of its own reputation.

facts.t: The Court reversed itself within months on retrospective clearances
facts.d: Vanashakti struck down ex post facto environmental clearances in May 2025. On review, a 2:1 bench recalled the judgment. Justice Bhuyan's dissent called it a retrogression from the precautionary principle.

facts.t: Walking on a footpath is now a fundamental right
facts.d: Maniyar Iliyaz held that safe, demarcated footpaths fall under Article 19(1)(d) with an Article 21 dimension — and that pedestrian movement takes priority over vehicular traffic. A right most Indian cities are structurally unable to honour.

bank.q: Harish Rana v. UoI is significant because it was:
o: The first case to recognise passive euthanasia
The first actual application of Common Cause (2018)
The first to permit active euthanasia
The first to recognise advance medical directives
bank.e: Aruna Shanbaug first recognised passive euthanasia and Common Cause validated living wills; Harish Rana was the first order actually implementing withdrawal, holding CANH to be medical treatment.

bank.q: With reference to Dr Jaya Thakur v. UoI, consider the following statements:
s: Menstrual health and dignity were located in Articles 21, 21A and 14.
The Court directed infrastructure, education and gender-sensitised curricula.
It mandated uniform paid menstrual leave nationwide.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. In the separate Shailendra Mani Tripathi petition the Court declined to mandate paid menstrual leave, fearing hiring bias, and referred the design to the Ministry.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (subject):
pairs: 2. A constitutional right to rehabilitation for trafficking victims
4. Forced narco tests violate Articles 20(3) and 21
bank.e: Prajwala on rehabilitation, Ranjitsinh on corporate environmental duty, Amlesh Kumar reaffirming Selvi, and Hamsaanandini Nanduri on adoptive maternity leave.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the demolition guidelines case?
o: Punitive demolitions were held wholly unconstitutional
Pan-India guidelines require show-cause notice, fifteen days and videography
Compensation of ₹10 lakh was ordered in March 2025
The Court held that municipal authorities have unfettered discretion in enforcement
bank.e: The whole point of the ruling was to subject demolition to due process, the separation of powers and the right to shelter under Articles 19 and 21.

bank.as: The Waqf (Amendment) Act interim order is described as a calibrated model of review.
bank.rs: The Court refused a blanket stay on the presumption of constitutionality while staying specific provisions.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — restraint at the level of the statute combined with protection at the level of particular provisions.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about Hamsaanandini Nanduri:
s: It struck down section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020.
It granted twelve weeks' leave irrespective of the adopted child's age.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Court urged the Centre to legislate on paternity leave; it did not mandate it.

bank.q: In the Aravalli hills matter the Court ultimately:
o: Upheld its 100 metre and 500 metre buffer definition unchanged
Stayed its own order and constituted a fresh High-Powered Expert Committee
Referred the matter to the National Green Tribunal
bank.e: After protests it stayed its own order and set up a fresh expert committee, with the interim mining freeze continuing.

bank.q: All of the following involved suo motu cognisance EXCEPT:
o: In Re: City Hounded by Strays
In Re: Illegal Sand Mining in National Chambal Sanctuary
bank.e: That was a petition. The other three were initiated by the Court on its own motion.

bank.q: In the Bihar Special Intensive Revision case, the Court:
o: Struck down the revision as beyond the ECI's powers
Upheld it under Article 324 and section 21(3) of the RPA while issuing rights-protective interim directions
Referred the matter to a Constitution Bench
Stayed the entire electoral roll revision
bank.e: Deference on the plenary power, combined with tailoring — Aadhaar and ration cards accepted as identification and online claims permitted for excluded voters.

bank.q: With reference to Article 142 in the 2025–26 docket, consider the following:
s: It was used in the Phalodi road-safety matter for nationwide interim directions.
A five-judge bench used it to lay down seniority rules for the Higher Judicial Service.
It was used to recall the Vanashakti judgment.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Vanashakti was recalled through the review jurisdiction, not Article 142.

bank.q: Amlesh Kumar v. State of Bihar reaffirmed which earlier decision on narco analysis?
bank.e: Selvi (2010). Voluntary tests require magistrate-recorded consent and carry no standalone evidentiary value.

bank.as: Several 2025–26 rulings are described as continuing mandamus in action.
bank.rs: The Court retained supervision through multi-stage proceedings with escalating directions rather than disposing of the matter at one hearing.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the stray dogs, Chambal sand mining and demolition matters all follow this pattern.
